placements.why: The envelope is an observatory instrument calibration record (Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates) — a distinct organizational-record subject (calibration status/verification) that neither the empty strata list nor any existing category holds. Nothing close exists to extend, so this is minted standalone as the foundational category this and future calibration envelopes will nest under.
placements.title: Instrument calibration becomes an organizational record category
placements.frame: Does this content establish or attest an instrument's calibration status as part of the org's operational record, rather than describing a product, strategy, or architecture decision?

placements.title: Calibration status becomes an attested, verified record rather than an asserted claim
placements.frame: Was this instrument's calibration independently verified against a named reference standard, and across what operating range does that verification hold?
placements.why: All three segments converge on the same thematic subject — the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration is not merely stated but verified against a named external reference (June reference plates) and shown to hold across the full observing band. This is a recurring subject future calibration envelopes for this or other instruments will keep feeding (verification-against-reference-standard as the pattern), not a one-time fact — the 88.4 MHz figure and the June-plates check are the evidence, not the leaf itself. No existing narrative leaf exists in this empty graph to hold it, so it is minted under the newly-placed Calibration strata.
